title: Why Can’t You Tickle Yourself?
description:
Your fingers make the same movement, but your brain turns down the sensation.

Prediction. The brain anticipates the sensory result of self-generated movement and attenuates it.

Motor commands produce an internal prediction; when expected and actual touch match, somatosensory activity is reduced.

Adding a delay between your movement and the touch can make self-produced stimulation feel more ticklish.
